newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgo-French GSM operator Mobistar to hike capital.
newsitem.headline: Belgo-French GSM operator Mobistar to hike capital.

text.p: Belgian-French company Mobistar, which operates Belgium's second GSM mobile phone network, said on Friday it would raise its capital by two billion Belgian francs in 1997.

"For the further development of the network, Mobistar will, in line with the business plan, proceed to a capital increase of two billion francs in 1997," Belgian data communications company Telinfo said in a statement.
Telinfo has 10 percent of Mobistar, which is owned 62 percent by France Telecom. A group of eight other Belgian investors has 28 percent.
Telinfo said it would finance its share of the capital increase with its own cash flow.
Mobistar has signed up 68,000 subscribers four months after its launch, 42,000 more than expected.
Asked whether Telinfo might increase its stake in Mobistar, Cordier said he was satisfied with 10 percent.
"Mobistar is a very good investment but perhaps there are other objectives we have to aim for," he said.
Cordier declined to give details on acquisition plans but said Telinfo was also trying to see how it could become number one -- in corporate data communications -- in other countries.
"Data communications is still unexplored territory," he said.
He said Telinfo had a market share of about 65 percent in Belgium and between 75 and 80 percent in Luxembourg where the state, European Union and major banks were among its clients.
Cordier said Mobistar was also only due to pay dividends to investors after four years.
